subject: Equality of Factor covariance of two latent factors for multiple groups

messages.author: 0c6ee837932f3ce3
messages.subject: Equality of Factor covariance of two latent factors for multiple groups
parts:
Dear all,

I want to apply a model based approach to handle nonignorable missing data (Holman & Glas, 2005).

For this I have a dataframe with the binary values of an ability test which measure the ability xsi and for each item a binary indicator (1=missing,0=not missing) meant to measure the latent missing propensity theta.

The mirt model be would e.g. be specified as followed:

mirt.mod <- "

theta = 1-20
xsi = 21-40

COV = xsi*theta
"

Through the joint distribution of theta and xsi the obtained xsi estimates will be weighted by theta. This should lead to adjusted xsi estimates if there is a relation between theta and xsi (Missingness is related to ability).

This approach assumes that the covariance for different groups (e.g. male/female) is equal.

What I would now be interested in is investigating if the relation between theta and xsi is equal for both groups.

This ist because both groups vary clearly in the mean of missing values, but it is unclear if the theta values used to weight xsi have to be identical or should be different for the groups.

I thought for this I should constrain the covariance to be equal between groups and compare this model to a model where the covariance is estimated freely for both groups.

As I found no clear information on how to do this, I would like to ask if any of you know If this is possible through e.g. CONSTRAINB or something similar?

Thanks for your support.

Bests
Indariel

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Equality of Factor covariance of two latent factors for multiple groups
parts:
Hi Indariel,

It is possible to implement this using the mirt.model() syntax. There is a keyword GROUP that can be used to access the latent variable hyper-parameters, so combined with the CONSTRAINB specification you should be able to achieve the equality via

syntax <- "...
  CONSTRAINB = (GROUP, COV_12)"

HTH.

Phil
